title: HTTP, credentials and endpoint authority
summary: HTTP requests are allow-listed evidence. Credential material is resolved only at the transport boundary and must not become CivicRequest, journal, cache, SQL or Runtime evidence. Endpoint authority and credential authority are distinct.
invariants: Caller Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie headers are forbidden.
Credential references may be retained; secret values may not.
Cache identity is partitioned by non-secret credential reference where authorization can affect representation.
Credential/local-policy failure cannot be converted into stale authorized success.
Companies House live and sandbox are separate host/credential/API/SQL domains even though they share the same response mapping generation.
AVWX bearer-token integration is a planned source candidate only; it is not implemented in CivicPort v0.14.
procedure: Bind credentials to exact allowed hosts.
Resolve secret values only inside the transport implementation and remove temporary material after use.
For sandbox/test environments, define a separate source identity and credential reference rather than a base-URL override that can cross credentials.
Never place bearer/API secrets in URL query parameters because URLs are retained evidence/cache identity.

provenance.claim: Credential references, cache partitioning, Companies House transport-only secret handling, Runtime and SQL boundaries.
Companies House live and sandbox are separate endpoint and credential domains.
